newsitem.title: UK: S&P expects to upgrade Ciba-Geigy to AAA.
newsitem.headline: S&P expects to upgrade Ciba-Geigy to AAA.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it expected to upgrade Ciba-Geigy Ltd's senior debt rating to AAA with a stable outlook upon successful completion of a merger with Sandoz Ltd.

"The senior debt ratings of Ciba-Geigy Ltd (Ciba) and related entities remain on CreditWatch with positive implications, where they were placed March 7, 1996 following the announcement of a merger agreement between Ciba and Sandoz Ltd," S&P said in a statement.
"The transaction is structured as a merger of equals based on an exchange of shares," it said.

"The future upgrade to AAA reflects an improvement in the combined group's business position in conjunction with the conservative financing of the transaction giving the new group one of the best financial profiles in the pharmaceutical industry," S&P said.
Future ratings will be based on the credit quality of a newly created company, Novartis Ltd, which will absorb the rated entities, Sandoz and Ciba, the agency said.
Potential divestments in crop protection and animal health are not expected to materially affect the overall transaction or the combined group's business position, S&P said.
S&P said from a business risk perspective Novartis --
-- combines two superior players in industries with generally favorable risk characteristics,

-- will have leading positions globally in pharmaceuticals, self-medication, optics, opthalmics, medical nutrition and in agrochemicals, making the combined entity the number one player in life sciences,

-- and will improve their health care business position via a larger portfolio of ethical drugs and self-medication products, a better therapeutic coverage, and improved critical mass in terms of marketing and R&D effort.
"Novartis will be better prepared to meet the challenges, such as healthcare reforms, facing the pharmaceuticals industry.

"The other business areas of Novartis all enjoy leading positions, and have synergies with healthcare. The disposal of their chemical units will also make the combined entity less cyclical than previously," S&P said.

In contrast to most mergers in the industry, the conservative all paper financing does not impair the combined group's already strong financial posture, it said, and the combination will have less debt than cash.

"The group's leading business positions in conjunction with its superior cash-generating ability and financial posture, continuation of a conservative track record regarding financial policies, merger synergies and cost-cutting potential, and financial flexibility stemming from asset disposals should enable the group to maintain its superior ratings," S&P said.
"Conversely, material changes in financial policies, its financial posture or to the merger arrangements, although not anticipated, would put pressure on the ratings," it said.
